what_happened: The job to define each site term once and link to it elsewhere was rejected at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: the git diff must show intro.json (and any site.rs template text) no longer restates definitions in the overview 'what' list, walkthrough steps, t4/t10 summaries or the limits list. There were two major findings and no blockers. First, two definitions are still repeated almost word for word in studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json (what[4] and limits[6]). Second, the test each_term_is_defined_once_and_every_term_link_resolves in xtask/src/site.rs only catches exact copies of a definition sentence, so a lightly reworded copy passes. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: The criterion asks for a non-repetition property that is fuzzy (near-duplicate text), but the producer's test only detects exact duplicate sentences. The producer therefore believed it was done once the test passed. Nothing in the job compared the test's matching strength with the criterion's wording, and nothing scanned the real intro.json for near-copies before the final verdict. The gap between what the check proves and what the criterion demands was found only by the verifier.
other_causes: The test's exact-sentence matching was too weak to serve as evidence for a criterion about restated definitions.
The data file has many places that carry definitions (what list, steps, summaries, limits list), and the producer missed two of them.
open_hypotheses: The given fields do not show whether the producer ran out of time or simply did not look at what[4] and limits[6].
It is unknown whether a looser near-duplicate check would flag legitimate text too.
contradictions: The registry class for unmet criteria at final verification fits, but the event also has a soundness finding about a weak test, which partly resembles criteria that check presence rather than behavior.
prevention: Add a default for jobs whose criterion is about removing repeated or near-duplicate text. The producer must list every place a term is defined or described, and before finishing must search the real files for reworded copies, such as by shared key phrases. Any test added for the criterion must also be shown to fail on a reworded copy. This would catch the leftover repeats before the verifier does.
